thread:
support-lead: FYI customer 'FinSight' is seeing p95/p99 spikes from eu-west clients to our hosted API starting ~15:12 UTC. Reports TLS handshake + connect time up to 700ms. Raised via support ticket #6789. Escalating to oncall.

maria-oncall: on it. do we have traces? any sudden deploys? @ajay-netops can you grab geo traces and dns history for their requests?

support-lead: no deploys on record during window. attached example curl from customer: 
```
curl -w "time_connect:%{time_connect}\ntime_appconnect:%{time_appconnect}\n" -o /dev/null -s "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate"
# time_connect:0.123\n# time_appconnect:0.623 (sometimes shows 0.5-0.7)
```

ajay-netops: pulling netlogs now. I see a small burst of EU->NA egress shifting between POPs at 15:11:58 -> 15:13:10. GSLB weights changed by traffic steering around that time (automated). Digging into DNS TTLs and any recent cartography changes.

kevin-runtime: i can correlate tracing. sample request id from ticket: req_01H2XYZ. tracing shows most time in socket connect + tls handshake span. Backend processing negligible.

ajay-netops: traceroute from eu-west peeks:
```
traceroute to api.redwood.example (34.72.110.91), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  0.9 ms  0.8 ms  0.7 ms
 2  198.51.100.5  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.3 ms
 3  203.0.113.10  50.2 ms  48.9 ms  52.1 ms
 4  34.72.110.91  250.6 ms  260.1 ms  255.3 ms
```
That 3->4 hop shows an unexpected long-haul path jump (~200ms). Also seeing intermittent SNI path mismatch logs on ingress LB.

maria-oncall: SNI mismatch? give me the ingress logs snippet. any TLS errors / earlyclose?

kevin-runtime: ingress logs for req_01H2XYZ: 
```
[15:12:05.112] conn_open src=198.51.100.10:43210 dst=34.72.110.91:443 tls_handshake=0.58s full_request=0.63s sni=api.redwood.example route=eu-west-pop-2
[15:12:05.680] conn_open src=198.51.100.10:43228 dst=34.72.110.91:443 tls_handshake=0.51s full_request=0.54s sni=api.redwood.example route=eu-central-pop-1
```
We have some requests hitting different POPs with varying handshake times.

ajay-netops: digging DNS history: at 15:11:45 our GSLB automated weight rebalancer flipped a small percentage of eu-west traffic to us-east for capacity smoothing. TTL for response A records is 20s. That explains client-perceived flapping for some clients. Looks like a subset experienced long-haul routing to NA POPs causing handshake tail.

maria-oncall: so root cause likely automated weight shift -> some clients route to NA POP -> long cross-region TCP/TLS -> p95/p99 spike. Can we confirm by correlating client ASN?

ajay-netops: yes. ASN grouping shows affected traffic primarily from a few ISPs in Ireland/Portugal that prefer particular exit nodes; their local egress to public internet routed via a transit that had a bad path to NA. Means our GSLB choice exposed them to a suboptimal path.

kevin-runtime: mitigation options:
- rollback GSLB weight change to prior steady config (quick).
- increase TTL to 60s to avoid rapid flapping (slower).
- add regional steering policy to pin EU-origin IPs to EU POPs for 5m window.

maria-oncall: immediate action: rollback weights to previous snapshot now and enable emergency pinning for eu-west prefixes for 10m. I’ll run rollback. @ajay-netops please prepare a short-lived route pin patch.

ajay-netops: applying rollback now. patch id: patch-gslb-17425-rollback. Rolling back 3% traffic that was shifted.

sre-bot: Deploy triggered: patch-gslb-17425-rollback started at 15:17:12 UTC.

kevin-runtime: after rollback, early checks show p95 fell from ~480ms to ~120ms within 40s for the sampled ASNs. Good signal.

maria-oncall: recording mitigation: rollback + pin. Will monitor for 30m then consider increasing TTL and a safe gating for future weight shifts. Also add canary that checks route RTT per ASN before shifting.

ajay-netops: note: rebalancer logic currently considers POP capacity and regional CPU, not ASN path health. I'll add an immediate TODO to include a simple RTT probe to candidate POPs from representative ASNs.

support-lead: customer updated: latency back to normal, they confirmed. Thanks for the fast response.

maria-oncall: follow-ups:
- postmortem entry (assign to ajay-netops)
- change request to rebalancer (ajay-netops)
- add ASN-based canary probes (kevin-runtime + ajay-netops)
- temporary TTL change discussion in infra-ops next week

ajay-netops: noted. I’ll stash logs and traceroutes into the incident bucket and open a PR for rebalancer guard.

maria-oncall: closing thread when postmortem is up. thanks all :thumbsup:
